topics.heading: Article 51A — Fundamental Duties
topics.summary: The Constitution lists eleven Fundamental Duties for every citizen. Four connect especially closely to Seewik’s civic-action routes.

sections.label: 51A(a)
sections.text: Abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem.

sections.label: 51A(b)
sections.text: Cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom.

sections.label: 51A(c)
sections.text: Uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India.

sections.label: 51A(d)
sections.text: Defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.

sections.label: 51A(e)
sections.text: Promote harmony and common brotherhood across religious, linguistic, regional and sectional differences, and renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.

sections.label: 51A(f)
sections.text: Value and preserve the rich heritage of India’s composite culture.

sections.label: 51A(g)
sections.text: Protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, and have compassion for living creatures.

sections.label: 51A(h)
sections.text: Develop scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.

sections.label: 51A(i)
sections.text: Safeguard public property and abjure violence.
links: Report a road, streetlight or public-toilet issue

sections.label: 51A(j)
sections.text: Strive towards excellence in individual and collective activity so the nation rises to higher levels of endeavour and achievement.

sections.label: 51A(k)
sections.text: As a parent or guardian, provide opportunities for education to a child or ward between six and fourteen years of age.

limitations: This page reproduces or plainly summarizes the constitutional duties; it does not give legal advice or decide whether a duty has been fulfilled.

sources.title: The Constitution of India, Part IVA, Article 51A

topics.heading: How municipal complaint follow-up works
topics.summary: A practical follow-up path is: the responsible municipal department, then the Chief Officer’s office, then a district or state public-grievance channel when municipal follow-up has failed.

sections.label: 1. Responsible department
sections.text: File through the confirmed municipal channel and keep the acknowledgement, date, photographs and any reply together.

sections.label: 2. Chief Officer’s office
sections.text: If the department does not respond, follow up with the municipal Chief Officer’s office. The Act places executive administration and supervision of municipal officers under the Chief Officer and provides for a Citizen’s Charter.

sections.label: 3. District or state grievance channel
sections.text: If the municipal route still fails, use the official public-grievance route for district or state administrative follow-up and attach the earlier record.

limitations: This is a plain-language follow-up sequence, not a statement that every complaint has a statutory appeal in this order.
Seewik does not file or escalate a complaint automatically.

topics.heading: Official civic recognition programmes
topics.summary: Some official programmes recognize cities, Good Samaritans or eligible volunteers. Their purpose and eligibility are different, so always check the programme page before acting on a reward claim.

sections.label: Swachh Survekshan 2025–26
sections.text: MoHUA’s urban cleanliness survey assesses urban local bodies and includes citizen feedback. Its main awards recognize cities and local bodies; participation does not create an automatic individual reward.

sections.label: Rah-Veer Good Samaritan scheme
sections.text: MoRTH’s revised guidelines, effective 21 April 2025, describe a ₹25,000 award for an eligible Good Samaritan who saves the life of a victim of a fatal motor-vehicle accident through immediate assistance during the golden hour. Official eligibility and district appraisal rules control the award.

sections.label: MY Bharat
sections.text: The Government of India platform lists volunteering and experiential-learning opportunities and offers digital recognition. Eligibility, selection and certificates depend on the individual programme.

limitations: Seewik does not determine eligibility, promise a reward, nominate a citizen or verify completion for any external programme.

topics.heading: What the Nagar Parishad works on
topics.summary: Nagar Parishad, Municipal Council and municipality refer to the urban local body. The Maharashtra Act assigns councils obligatory municipal duties within their municipal area.

sections.label: Public streets and lighting
sections.text: Lighting public streets, maintaining and cleaning public streets, and handling defined street obstructions and municipal road work.

sections.label: Waste, sanitation and drainage
sections.text: Cleaning streets and sewers, removing filth, maintaining drains and sewers, and providing public conveniences.

sections.label: Water and public health
sections.text: Municipal water-supply duties, sanitation measures and certain public-health functions within the council’s legal scope.

sections.label: Public spaces and environment
sections.text: Maintaining municipal public places and carrying out environmental-protection functions assigned to the council.

limitations: Not every issue inside Nandurbar district belongs to the Nagar Parishad; highways, rural areas and district/state assets may have a different authority.
Future Nagar Parishad campaign tracking is not included in this first version.
